```{r load}
library(wet)
library(ggplot2)
sf::sf_use_s2(FALSE)

# This article runs on saved outputs: data-raw/segment_vignette_data.R reads the
# gauge values from the published parts and checks each against its source,
# data-raw/segment_vignette_map.R reads the picked source of every segment from
# the same build, and data-raw/monthly_vignette_data.R reads the three Bulkley
# segments' months and days and the gauges' held-out months from it; each
# records the commits and reports it came from
vd <- function(f) system.file("vignette-data", f, package = "wet")
vs <- readRDS(vd("segment_values.rds"))
ps <- vs$provenance
pub <- ps$published
vm <- readRDS(vd("monthly_values.rds"))
pm <- vm$provenance
map <- readRDS(vd("segment_map.rds"))
bc <- readRDS(vd("station_map.rds"))$bc
bmap <- readRDS(vd("monthly_map.rds"))
daily <- readRDS(vd("station_daily.rds"))
lh <- utils::read.csv(vd("life_history_bulk.csv"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE, na.strings = "")

# the values below are the published product's, checked against what they
# were built from (none may differ), and the map's picks are the same build's
stopifnot(identical(pub$manifest, wet:::wet_catalog_url), all(ps$published_check$compared > 0),
          all(ps$published_check$differing == 0),
          identical(map$provenance$published$wet_commit, pub$wet_commit),
          identical(map$provenance$published$built, pub$built),
          # the closing section gives one read date for the gauge values and the map
          identical(map$provenance$built, ps$built))
# the Bulkley values were each checked against what they were built from by
# data-raw/monthly_vignette_data.R (the rest rest on the publish report): none may differ
stopifnot(identical(pm$published$manifest, wet:::wet_catalog_url), all(pm$published_check$compared > 0),
          all(pm$published_check$differing == 0))
# the closing section names one build, one read date, one fit and one routed run
# for both bundles
stopifnot(identical(pm$published$wet_commit, pub$wet_commit), identical(pm$published$built, pub$built),
          identical(pm$published$report, pub$report), identical(pm$built, ps$built),
          identical(pm$province_run, ps$province_run), identical(pm$hydat_release, ps$hydat_release),
          identical(pm$aet, ps$aet),
          identical(pm$routed_commit, ps$routed_commit), identical(pm$routed, ps$routed))
# the prose gives routed's period from the published rows; the balance's is 1981-2010
stopifnot(length(ps$routed_period) == 1, grepl(ps$routed_period, ps$routed, fixed = TRUE))

# colours come from the gq registries, so no hex literal appears in this
# vignette; assert each class set, because a malformed CSV row adds a layer silently
reg <- gq::gq_reg_custom(system.file("cartography", "wet_segment.csv", package = "wet"))
reg_st <- gq::gq_reg_custom(system.file("cartography", "wet_station.csv", package = "wet"))
classes <- function(r, layer, expect) {
  x <- gq::gq_tmap_classes(r$layers[[layer]])
  stopifnot(identical(names(x$values), expect))
  list(values = x$values, labels = stats::setNames(x$labels, names(x$values)))
}
pal_pick <- classes(reg, "pick_source", c("pcic_routed", "wet_balance"))
pal_gauge <- classes(reg, "gauge", "calibration")
pal_outline <- classes(reg, "segment_map", "outline")
pal_src <- classes(reg, "flow_source", c("observed", "pcic_routed", "wet_balance"))
pal_hydro <- classes(reg_st, "hydrograph", c("band", "median", "window"))

theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
            theme(legend.position = "bottom", panel.grid.minor = element_blank()))
pct <- function(x) paste0(round(x), "%")
pct1 <- function(x) paste0(format(round(x, 1), nsmall = 1), "%")
# signed whole percents, with a zero that rounds from either side printed as 0%
signed <- function(x, d = 0) {
  s <- sub("^[+-](0(\\.0+)?%)$", "\\1", sprintf(paste0("%+.", d, "f%%"), x))
  sub("^-", "−", s)
}
num <- function(x, d = 0) format(round(x, d), big.mark = ",", nsmall = d)
and_text <- function(x) if (length(x) < 2) x else paste(paste(x[-length(x)], collapse = ", "), "and", x[length(x)])
to_title <- function(x) {
  vapply(strsplit(tolower(x), " "), function(w) {
    big <- !w %in% c("at", "the", "near", "of", "in", "above", "below", "north")
    w[big] <- paste0(toupper(substring(w[big], 1, 1)), substring(w[big], 2))
    paste(w, collapse = " ")
  }, "")
}
# stopifnot(logical(0)) passes, so a lookup that can come back empty is checked
one <- function(x) {
  stopifnot(length(x) == 1, !is.na(x))
  x
}
gh <- function(path) paste0("https://github.com/NewGraphEnvironment/wet/blob/main/", path)

sk <- vs$skill
sg <- vs$segments
bs <- vm$segments
g <- vm$gauges
days <- c(365.25, wet_month_days())
base <- 1981:2010
base_text <- paste0(min(base), "–", max(base))
period_of <- function(src) unique(bs$period[bs$source == src])
# the product spells a period with a hyphen; the prose with an en dash. The
# prose says both sources cover the gauges' period
stopifnot(identical(period_of("wet_balance"), paste0(min(base), "-", max(base))),
          identical(period_of("pcic_routed"), period_of("wet_balance")),
          identical(ps$routed_period, period_of("pcic_routed")))
```

```{r product}
parts <- pub$parts
ds <- function(x) paste0("discharge/fwa/v1/", x)
seg_parts <- parts[parts$dataset == ds("segment_monthly"), ]
ws_parts <- parts[parts$dataset == ds("watershed_monthly"), ]
day_parts <- parts[parts$dataset == ds("segment_daily"), ]
reader <- pub$reader
# the three datasets, only the balance in the watershed table, and every
# daily part one watershed group's
stopifnot(nrow(seg_parts) + nrow(ws_parts) + nrow(day_parts) == nrow(parts), all(ws_parts$source == "wet_balance"),
          setequal(day_parts$source, c("pcic_routed", "wet_balance")), all(grepl("^[A-Z]{4}$", day_parts$code)),
          setequal(seg_parts$source, c("pcic_routed", "wet_balance")),
          sum(seg_parts$rows) == sum(reader$rows))
# segments with each source (13 rows each), and with both
n_src <- stats::setNames(reader$rows / 13, reader$source)
n_with <- sg[["pick_routed"]] + sg[["pick_balance"]]
n_both_src <- sum(n_src) - n_with
stopifnot(all(n_src == round(n_src)))
# the prose: almost every stream has an estimate (99.9% of the segments linked to
# a watershed polygon in fwa_streams_watersheds_lut; an unlinked segment is in no
# source's table, as segment_output.R builds both from the linked set), the
# unlinked almost all connection lines and secondary channels (the Limits
# bullet), and the balance covers almost all of BC
own_pct <- 100 * (sg[["fwa"]] - sg[["neither"]]) / (sg[["fwa"]] - sg[["no_lut"]])
stopifnot(sg[["no_lut"]] <= sg[["neither"]], round(own_pct, 1) == 99.9,
          sg[["no_lut_connector"]] > 0.9 * sg[["no_lut"]], n_src[["wet_balance"]] > 0.9 * sg[["fwa"]])
built <- as.Date(substr(pub$built, 1, 10))
built_text <- paste(as.integer(format(built, "%d")), format(built, "%B %Y"))

stations <- c("08EE013", "08EE003", "08EE004")
# the prose: the balance's months add up to its month 0
bal_seg <- bs[bs$source == "wet_balance", ]
bal_sum <- vapply(stations, function(s) {
  x <- bal_seg[bal_seg$station_number == s & bal_seg$month > 0, ]
  sum(x$q_m3s * days[x$month + 1]) / sum(days[-1])
}, 0)
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(unname(bal_sum),
                           bal_seg$q_m3s[bal_seg$month == 0][match(stations, bal_seg$station_number[bal_seg$month == 0])])))
# the prose names the donor shares and the snow terms they are matched on:
# the fit must have shipped both
stopifnot(identical(pm$share_spec, "snow"), identical(pm$share_method, "donor"))
```

## What it is

The R package [`wet`](https://newgraphenvironment.github.io/wet/) [@irvine2026wetStream] publishes the mean
flow of British Columbia's Freshwater Atlas stream segments, in cubic metres
per second, for the year, each month and each day. Few streams in BC have a
gauge, so this gives almost every one of them an estimate: what flow a stream
carries in the weeks a fish needs it, and how that compares with the next
stream. Each value comes from one of two sources, and the map shows which one
a reader gets by default on BC's larger rivers.

```{r map-pick-data}
mp <- map$provenance
rv <- map$rivers[map$rivers$class != "none", ]
order_width <- c(`5` = 0.12, `6` = 0.22, `7` = 0.35, `8` = 0.55)
rv$w <- order_width[as.character(rv$order_band)]
stopifnot(!anyNA(rv$w))
gpts <- sf::st_transform(sf::st_as_sf(sk, coords = c("lon", "lat"), crs = 4326), 3005)
bb_bc <- gq::gq_bbox_aspect(sf::st_bbox(bc), asp = 7 / 5.8)
dx_bc <- bb_bc[["xmax"]] - bb_bc[["xmin"]]
dy_bc <- bb_bc[["ymax"]] - bb_bc[["ymin"]]
sb_bc_km <- max(gq::gq_scale_breaks(bb_bc))
sb_bc <- data.frame(x = bb_bc[["xmin"]] + 0.05 * dx_bc, y = bb_bc[["ymin"]] + 0.05 * dy_bc)
sb_bc$xend <- sb_bc$x + sb_bc_km * 1000
lab <- cbind(sf::st_coordinates(map$regions), name = map$regions$name)
lab <- data.frame(x = as.numeric(lab[, "X"]), y = as.numeric(lab[, "Y"]), name = lab[, "name"])
drawn <- sum(mp$drawn[names(mp$drawn) != "none"])
stopifnot(setequal(names(mp$drawn), c("none", "pcic_routed", "wet_balance")))
cap_pick <- sprintf(paste(
  "The source of the default flow (`pick`, under \"Which value to use\") on main-flow rivers of stream order %d",
  "and up (wider for higher orders), %s of",
  "BC's segments, and the %d calibration gauges. Smaller streams are not drawn, nor the few (under 1%%) of",
  "that order with neither. Labels name the Liard and the Nechako Reservoir; the scale bar is %d km."
), mp$min_order, pct(100 * drawn / sg[["fwa"]]), nrow(sk), sb_bc_km)
stopifnot(setequal(map$regions$name, c("Liard", "Nechako Reservoir")),
          mp$drawn[["none"]] < 0.01 * sum(mp$drawn))
```

```{r map-pick, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 6.6, fig.cap = cap_pick}
ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = bc, fill = "white", colour = pal_outline$values[["outline"]], linewidth = 0.25) +
  geom_sf(data = rv, aes(colour = class, linewidth = w)) +
  scale_linewidth_identity() +
  scale_colour_manual(values = pal_pick$values, labels = pal_pick$labels, name = NULL,
                      guide = guide_legend(override.aes = list(linewidth = 1.2))) +
  geom_sf(data = gpts, aes(shape = "calibration"), colour = pal_gauge$values[["calibration"]], size = 0.6) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(calibration = 16), labels = pal_gauge$labels, name = NULL,
                     guide = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size = 1.6))) +
  geom_label(data = lab, aes(x, y, label = name), size = 2.9, linewidth = 0, fill = "white", alpha = 0.8,
             label.padding = unit(1.5, "pt")) +
  geom_segment(data = sb_bc, aes(x = x, xend = xend, y = y, yend = y), linewidth = 1) +
  geom_text(data = sb_bc, aes(x = (x + xend) / 2, y = y, label = paste(sb_bc_km, "km")), vjust = -0.7, size = 3) +
  coord_sf(xlim = bb_bc[c("xmin", "xmax")], ylim = bb_bc[c("ymin", "ymax")], expand = FALSE, datum = NA) +
  theme_void() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.text = element_text(size = 9),
        panel.border = element_rect(fill = NA, colour = pal_outline$values[["outline"]], linewidth = 0.3))
```

It is public, in three datasets:

- **`segment_monthly`**: each segment's flow from each source, for the year
  (month 0) and the twelve calendar months.
- **`watershed_monthly`**: the same per fundamental watershed, the small
  polygon each segment drains, from the water balance only.
- **`segment_daily`**: `segment_monthly` per day (29 February folded into 28).

Each row comes from one of two sources, both over `r base_text`:

**Routed PCIC** (`pcic_routed`). The Pacific Climate Impacts
Consortium (PCIC) at the University of Victoria models runoff with VIC-GL
[@schnorbus2018VICGlacierVICGL] and routes it down its rivers with Raven
[@craig_etal2020Flexiblewatershed], published as
[hydromosaic](https://beehive.pacificclimate.org/chyp/). New Graph's
[fork](https://github.com/NewGraphEnvironment/fwapg/tree/newgraph) of the PostgreSQL tools
[`fwapg`](https://github.com/smnorris/fwapg) [@norris2024smnorrisfwapg; @norris_irvine2026NewGraphEnvironmentfwapg]
places that flow on Freshwater Atlas segments, as
[the fork's notes](https://github.com/NewGraphEnvironment/fwapg/blob/newgraph/research/pcic_routed_flow_periods.md)
set out.

**Open water balance** (`wet_balance`). `wet`'s own estimate, after
@chapman_etal2018Wateralloc:
precipitation less actual evapotranspiration from climate normals, averaged
over each watershed's upstream area and adjusted per
[hydrologic zone](https://catalogue.data.gov.bc.ca/dataset/bc-hydrologic-zones)
against the Water Survey of Canada's
[HYDAT](https://www.canada.ca/en/environment-climate-change/services/water-overview/quantity/monitoring/survey/data-products-services/national-archive-hydat.html)
gauges. The year is split into months by the shares of the year carried by
the five gauges most like the place, matched on elevation, location and snow
(`wet_share_fit()`), and each month into days by the same gauges' pattern, so
its days average to its months and its months add up to its year. It covers
almost all of BC, and its code and inputs are open.

Neither is the gauge record.

## Which value to use

```{r pick}
rg <- sf::st_drop_geometry(map$regions)
rownames(rg) <- rg$name
liard <- rg["Liard", ]
nech <- rg["Nechako Reservoir", ]
nech_bal <- 100 * nech$wet_balance / (nech$wet_balance + nech$pcic_routed)
# the prose: routed has no value in the Liard, so the balance is picked there;
# on the Nechako Reservoir it is picked on nearly every segment; the cut is a fifth;
# and most segments have both sources
stopifnot(liard$pcic_routed == 0, liard$wet_balance > 0, nech_bal > 90, ps$far_low == 0.2,
          sg[["far_low"]] > 0, n_both_src > 0.5 * sg[["fwa"]],
          # the balance is picked where routed is far low, and otherwise only where routed has none
          sg[["pick_balance"]] - sg[["far_low"]] == n_src[["wet_balance"]] - n_both_src)
pct_of <- function(n) pct(100 * n / sg[["fwa"]])
```

Most segments, `r pct_of(n_both_src)`, have a value from both sources, and the two
differ, so one row per segment is marked as the default with `pick`. It is
chosen once per segment, on annual flow, and the same source is picked for
every month and day:

- **routed PCIC**, where it has a value;
- **the balance** where routed PCIC's annual flow is under a fifth of the
  balance's on a segment that lies on its own watershed's line. Off that
  line (side channels, and connectors and waterbody connections the lookup
  gives another line's watershed), routed PCIC is kept however low it is;
- **whichever has a value**, where only one does.

`pick` takes routed PCIC on `r pct_of(sg[["pick_routed"]])` of the Freshwater
Atlas's segments and the balance on `r pct_of(sg[["pick_balance"]])`:
on `r pct_of(sg[["far_low"]])` of all segments because routed flow is far low there, and on the rest because routed PCIC has none. The balance takes every segment with a value in the Liard, where
routed PCIC has none, and `r pct(nech_bal)` of those in the four Nechako
Reservoir groups, where routed flow is far below the balance's.

## How to read it

`wet` knows where the parts are, so reading a stream takes its
`linear_feature_id` and its watershed group. The parts are sorted by group,
so naming it lets [`duckdb`](https://r.duckdb.org/) [@muhleisen_raasveldt2026duckdb] skip everything outside
it, and the read takes seconds; the months can be read without it, and the
days cannot:

```{r read, echo = TRUE, eval = FALSE}
library(wet)
# Buck Creek at its mouth, where gauge 08EE013 sits
q <- wet_segment_monthly(NULL, 17094080, groups = "BULK")

# twelve months a column per source
reshape(q[q$month > 0, c("source", "month", "q_m3s")], idvar = "month",
        timevar = "source", direction = "wide")
```

```{r read-check}
# the recipes are run as written by the data scripts, on this segment; a
# routed row carries no coverage
stopifnot(all(is.na(bs$coverage[bs$source == "pcic_routed"])))
stopifnot(identical(unique(bs$linear_feature_id[bs$station_number == "08EE013"]), 17094080L),
          vs$daily$segment == 17094080, identical(vs$daily$group, "BULK"), all(vs$daily$days$basis == "daily"),
          identical(vs$daily$window, data.frame(window = "spring", start = "04-15", end = "06-15")))
```

`wet_segment_monthly()` returns `linear_feature_id, month, q_m3s, source`,
the shape of `wet_station_monthly()`'s gauge record, so a comparison is a join
on `month`. A segment a source lacks comes back with `NA` months, not missing
rows. `wet_segment_daily()` reads a segment's days, and `wet_flow_window()` the
mean flow over a timing window from days or months:

```{r read-daily, echo = TRUE, eval = FALSE}
q <- wet_segment_daily(NULL, 17094080, groups = "BULK")
wet_flow_window(q, data.frame(window = "spring", start = "04-15", end = "06-15"))
```

A whole group's default annual flow is one query on the parts. `scenario`,
`forcing` and `source` are in each part's path, not the file, so read with
`hive_partitioning`:

```{r read-group, echo = TRUE, eval = FALSE}
cat <- wet_catalog()   # the manifest: one row per part, with its href
segs <- cat$href[cat$dataset == "discharge/fwa/v1/segment_monthly"]

duck <- DBI::dbConnect(duckdb::duckdb())
DBI::dbExecute(duck, "INSTALL httpfs; LOAD httpfs;")
DBI::dbGetQuery(duck, sprintf("
  SELECT linear_feature_id, source, q_m3s
  FROM read_parquet([%s], hive_partitioning = true)
  WHERE scenario = 'historical' AND watershed_group_code = 'BULK' AND month = 0 AND pick",
  paste0("'", segs, "'", collapse = ", ")))
```

Or load it into [`PostgreSQL`](https://www.postgresql.org/) beside the
Freshwater Atlas, where `wet_segment_monthly()` also reads it when given the
connection:

```{r read-db, echo = TRUE, eval = FALSE}
conn <- DBI::dbConnect(RPostgres::Postgres(), dbname = "fwapg")
wet_db_load(conn, cat)   # discharge.fwa_v1_segment_monthly
```

Besides flow (`q_m3s`) a row carries `runoff_mm`, the same water as a depth
over the area upstream (NA for a routed row off its watershed's own line),
`coverage`, the share of that area the balance's inputs cover (NA on a
routed row), and `period`.

## What a year looks like

```{r bulkley}
names_st <- c(stats::setNames(attr(daily, "provenance")$stations$station_name,
                              attr(daily, "provenance")$stations$station_number),
              stats::setNames(unique(g[c("station_number", "station_name")])$station_name,
                              unique(g[c("station_number", "station_name")])$station_number))
st_label <- stats::setNames(sprintf("%s (%s)", to_title(names_st[stations]), stations), stations)
ch <- lh[lh$species_code == "CH" & lh$life_stage %in% c("migration", "spawning", "fry_migration"), ]
stopifnot(nrow(ch) == 3, all(ch$end > ch$start))  # none crosses the new year
stage <- sub("_", " ", ch$life_stage)
windows <- data.frame(window = paste0(toupper(substring(stage, 1, 1)), substring(stage, 2)),
                      start = ch$start, end = ch$end)
# the table cites one source for the three windows, which the prose names
stopifnot(identical(unique(ch$source), "gottesfeld_rabnett2007SkeenaFish"))
md_text <- function(md) {
  d <- as.Date(paste0("2001-", md))
  paste(format(d, "%b"), as.integer(format(d, "%d")))
}
span_of <- function(w) {
  k <- one(which(windows$window == w))
  paste(md_text(windows$start[k]), "to", md_text(windows$end[k]))
}

# observed monthly means, 1981-2010: the calibration record (complete years)
# where the gauge is a calibration gauge, otherwise the daily record's
# month-years with at least 20 days of flow, in months that have 10 of them
obs_cal <- g[g$station_number %in% stations & g$month > 0, ]
obs_cal$q_m3s <- obs_cal$obs_mm * obs_cal$area_km2 * 1e6 / (days[obs_cal$month + 1] * 86400 * 1000)
min_days <- 20
min_years <- 10
dh <- daily[daily$source == "hydat", ]
dh$year <- as.integer(format(dh$date, "%Y"))
dh$month <- as.integer(format(dh$date, "%m"))
dh <- dh[dh$year %in% base, ]
my <- stats::aggregate(q_m3s ~ station_number + year + month, dh, function(q) c(mean = mean(q), n = length(q)))
my <- data.frame(my[c("station_number", "year", "month")], q = my$q_m3s[, "mean"], n = my$q_m3s[, "n"])
my <- my[my$n >= min_days, ]
obs_daily <- stats::aggregate(q ~ station_number + month, my, function(q) c(mean = mean(q), n = length(q)))
obs_daily <- data.frame(obs_daily[c("station_number", "month")], q_m3s = obs_daily$q[, "mean"],
                        n_years = obs_daily$q[, "n"])
obs_daily <- obs_daily[obs_daily$n_years >= min_years, ]
not_cal <- setdiff(stations, unique(g$station_number))
stopifnot(identical(not_cal, "08EE003"))
obs <- rbind(obs_cal[c("station_number", "month", "q_m3s", "n_years")],
             obs_daily[obs_daily$station_number %in% not_cal, ])
obs$source <- "observed"
# 08EE003 is seasonal: the months it has, and the years they come from
m003 <- sort(obs$month[obs$station_number == "08EE003"])
stopifnot(identical(m003, min(m003):max(m003)))
m003_text <- paste0(month.name[min(m003)], "–", month.name[max(m003)])
n003 <- length(unique(my$year[my$station_number == "08EE003" & my$month %in% m003]))
# the prose: 08EE003 has no complete year in 1981-2010 (every month with 20 days)
stopifnot(!any(table(my$year[my$station_number == "08EE003"]) == 12))

mid <- function(m) as.Date(sprintf("2001-%02d-15", m))
hyd <- rbind(bs[bs$month > 0, c("station_number", "month", "q_m3s", "source")],
             obs[c("station_number", "month", "q_m3s", "source")])
hyd$date <- mid(hyd$month)
hyd$source <- factor(hyd$source, names(pal_src$values))
hyd$station_number <- factor(hyd$station_number, stations, st_label[stations])

# the windows as strips under each panel, one row each
top <- stats::aggregate(q_m3s ~ station_number, hyd, max)
strip <- merge(top, data.frame(window = windows$window, row = seq_len(nrow(windows)),
                               start = as.Date(paste0("2001-", windows$start)),
                               end = as.Date(paste0("2001-", windows$end))), by = NULL)
strip$y <- -strip$q_m3s * (0.04 + 0.07 * (strip$row - 1)) - strip$q_m3s * 0.03
strip$h <- strip$q_m3s * 0.045
strip$label_x <- strip$end + 4

peak_month <- function(src) {
  x <- hyd[hyd$station_number == st_label[["08EE013"]] & hyd$source == src, ]
  one(x$month[which.max(x$q_m3s)])
}
stopifnot(peak_month("observed") == 5, peak_month("pcic_routed") == 5)
```

```{r geography}
# the prose: the three gauges nest (Buck Creek's FWA catchment inside Houston's,
# both inside Quick's), and the Bulkley flows north-west from the Houston gauge
# to the Quick gauge (BC Albers); catchments and gauge points from monthly_map.rds
catch <- bmap$catchments
area_in <- function(a, b) {
  ca <- sf::st_geometry(catch[catch$station_number == a, ])
  cb <- sf::st_geometry(catch[catch$station_number == b, ])
  stopifnot(length(ca) == 1, length(cb) == 1)
  # an empty intersection sums to 0, so two catchments that do not overlap fail
  sum(as.numeric(sf::st_area(sf::st_intersection(ca, cb)))) / as.numeric(sf::st_area(ca))
}
stopifnot(area_in("08EE013", "08EE003") > 0.99, area_in("08EE003", "08EE004") > 0.99)
xy_st <- sf::st_coordinates(bmap$stations)
rownames(xy_st) <- bmap$stations$station_number
stopifnot(xy_st["08EE004", "X"] < xy_st["08EE003", "X"], xy_st["08EE004", "Y"] > xy_st["08EE003", "Y"])
```

The Bulkley River, in west-central BC, flows north-west from Houston to join
the Skeena at Hazelton. Three gauges in its basin sit one inside the next.
Buck Creek joins the Bulkley at Houston; the Houston gauge sits just
downstream and measures it too, and the Quick gauge, further down, drains the
whole basin above. Buck Creek and Quick are among the gauges the water
balance is built on. Houston is not: it reads only in open water and has no
complete year in `r base_text`.

The strips under the hydrographs are chinook salmon life history timing
windows on the Bulkley, the weeks each life stage needs the river: adults
migrating upstream from `r span_of("Migration")`, spawning from
`r span_of("Spawning")`, and fry moving downstream from
`r span_of("Fry migration")`. They come from New Graph's species-timing table,
which cites @gottesfeld_rabnett2007SkeenaFish.

```{r hydro-cap}
cap_hyd <- paste0(
  "Mean monthly flow on the three gauges' segments from each source, beside the gauge's observed monthly ",
  "means over ", base_text, ". At ", st_label[["08EE003"]], ", a seasonal gauge, only the months with ",
  min_years, " or more years of ", min_days, " days' flow are drawn (", m003_text,
  "). The strips under each panel are the chinook life history timing windows."
)
```

```{r hydrographs, fig.height = 7.2, fig.cap = cap_hyd}
ggplot(hyd) +
  geom_rect(data = strip, aes(xmin = start, xmax = end, ymin = y - h / 2, ymax = y + h / 2),
            fill = pal_hydro$values[["window"]]) +
  geom_text(data = strip, aes(x = label_x, y = y, label = window), hjust = 0, size = 2.6, colour = "grey30") +
  geom_line(aes(date, q_m3s, colour = source), linewidth = 0.7) +
  geom_point(aes(date, q_m3s, colour = source), size = 1.2) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = pal_src$values, labels = pal_src$labels, name = NULL) +
  scale_x_date(date_breaks = "1 month", date_labels = "%b",
               limits = as.Date(c("2001-01-01", "2001-12-31")), expand = c(0.01, 0)) +
  facet_wrap(~station_number, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Mean flow (m³/s)")
```

```{r bulkley-numbers}
freshet <- function(s, src) {
  x <- hyd[hyd$station_number == st_label[[s]] & hyd$source == src & hyd$month %in% 5:6, ]
  sum(x$q_m3s * days[x$month + 1]) / sum(days[x$month + 1])
}
fr <- vapply(c("observed", "pcic_routed", "wet_balance"), function(src) freshet("08EE013", src), 0)
fr_q <- vapply(c("observed", "pcic_routed", "wet_balance"), function(src) freshet("08EE004", src), 0)
hq <- function(s, src, mo) {
  x <- hyd[hyd$station_number == st_label[[s]] & hyd$source == src & hyd$month %in% mo, ]
  stopifnot(nrow(x) == length(mo))
  x$q_m3s[match(mo, x$month)]
}
# the prose: at both calibration gauges the balance's months are the gauge's
# own monthly pattern (its nearest donor is itself) at the balance's annual
# flow, so every month is off by about the annual's error, and below the gauge;
# routed overshoots Buck Creek's freshet, and at Quick is above the gauge in
# July and August and short of it in May-June by a fifth to a third
ratio_of <- function(s) hq(s, "wet_balance", 1:12) / hq(s, "observed", 1:12)
wb_off <- vapply(c("08EE013", "08EE004"), function(s) 100 * (stats::median(ratio_of(s)) - 1), 0)
stopifnot(all(vapply(c("08EE013", "08EE004"), function(s) diff(range(ratio_of(s))) < 0.02, NA)),
          all(wb_off < 0), all(wb_off > -15),
          peak_month("wet_balance") == peak_month("observed"),
          all(hq("08EE004", "pcic_routed", 7:8) > hq("08EE004", "observed", 7:8)),
          fr[["pcic_routed"]] > fr[["observed"]], hq("08EE013", "pcic_routed", 5) > hq("08EE013", "observed", 5))
q_short <- 100 * (fr_q[["pcic_routed"]] / fr_q[["observed"]] - 1)
stopifnot(q_short < -20, q_short > -33)
```

Buck Creek peaks in May, and so does routed PCIC, which overshoots it: its
May–June flow is `r round(fr[["pcic_routed"]], 1)` m³/s against
`r round(fr[["observed"]], 1)` at the gauge. At Quick, routed PCIC is about a
quarter short in May–June (`r round(fr_q[["pcic_routed"]])` m³/s against
`r round(fr_q[["observed"]])`) and high in July and August.

At Buck Creek and Quick the balance's published months are in-sample: the
gauge most like each of them is itself, so the balance there has the gauge's
own monthly pattern at the balance's annual flow, about `r signed(wb_off[["08EE013"]])`
and `r signed(wb_off[["08EE004"]])` in every month. The scores below hold
each gauge out instead. At Houston the balance is a true estimate for an
ungauged site, and the gauge can check it only in open water.

## How good it is

```{r scores}
err_cut <- 20
band <- err_cut / 100
# a gauge whose segment carries under this share of its observed flow is left
# out of routed's scores, as the routed report leaves it out
# (scripts/pcic_routed_lib.R, routed_far_low)
far_low <- 0.2
a <- g[g$month == 0, ]
far <- a$station_number[!is.na(a$routed_mm) & a$routed_mm < far_low * a$obs_mm]
n_routed <- sum(!is.na(a$routed_mm))
# the two bundles hold the same gauges, observed and held-out runoff, and routed
# reaches the same ones: the yearly and monthly rows score one set
stopifnot(setequal(sk$station_number, a$station_number),
          isTRUE(all.equal(sk$obs, a$obs_mm[match(sk$station_number, a$station_number)])),
          isTRUE(all.equal(sk$mod, a$wb_mm[match(sk$station_number, a$station_number)])),
          identical(sort(sk$station_number[!is.na(sk$routed_mm)]), sort(a$station_number[!is.na(a$routed_mm)])),
          identical(sort(far), sort(sk$station_number[!is.na(sk$routed_mm) & sk$routed_mm < far_low * sk$obs])))

# yearly: mean annual runoff, error as a percentage of observed
ann <- sk[!is.na(sk$routed_mm) & !sk$station_number %in% far, ]
ann$rt_err <- 100 * (ann$routed_mm / ann$obs - 1)
n_both <- nrow(ann)
n_rt_closer <- sum(abs(ann$rt_err) < abs(ann$err_pct))
score <- function(e) {
  q <- stats::quantile(e, c(0.25, 0.75))
  c(mae = mean(abs(e)), bias = mean(e), lo = q[[1]], hi = q[[2]], within = 100 * mean(abs(e) <= err_cut))
}
s_rt <- score(ann$rt_err)
s_wb <- score(ann$err_pct)
s_all <- score(sk$err_pct)

# monthly: modelled over observed. A zero month is a ratio of 0 (an error of
# -100%), which ranks like any other, so the medians keep it
m <- g[g$month > 0, ]
m$ratio_wb <- m$wb_mm / m$obs_mm
m$ratio_r <- m$routed_mm / m$obs_mm
# no observed month is zero, so every ratio is defined. The balance at every
# calibration gauge; routed where its segment has flow, less the far-low ones
stopifnot(all(m$obs_mm > 0), !anyNA(m$ratio_wb))
bal <- m
both <- m[!is.na(m$routed_mm) & !m$station_number %in% far, ]
n_bal_gauges <- length(unique(bal$station_number))
n_both_gauges <- length(unique(both$station_number))
stopifnot(sum(bal$wb_mm <= 0) == 0, 12 * n_both_gauges == nrow(both), n_routed - length(far) == n_both_gauges,
          12 * n_bal_gauges == nrow(bal), !anyNA(both$ratio_r), n_both_gauges == n_both,
          setequal(unique(both$station_number), ann$station_number), n_bal_gauges == nrow(sk))
summ <- function(d, col, src) {
  do.call(rbind, lapply(split(d[[col]], d$month), function(r) {
    data.frame(source = src, median = 100 * (stats::median(r) - 1),
               q25 = 100 * (stats::quantile(r, 0.25, names = FALSE) - 1),
               q75 = 100 * (stats::quantile(r, 0.75, names = FALSE) - 1),
               within = 100 * mean(abs(r - 1) <= band))
  }))
}
# each source on its own gauges (the figure), and the balance on routed's (the table)
sm <- rbind(cbind(month = 1:12, summ(bal, "ratio_wb", "wet_balance")),
            cbind(month = 1:12, summ(both, "ratio_r", "pcic_routed")))
sh <- cbind(month = 1:12, summ(both, "ratio_wb", "wet_balance"))
smv <- function(src, mo, col) {
  x <- sm[[col]][sm$source == src & sm$month %in% mo]
  stopifnot(length(x) == length(mo), !anyNA(x))
  x
}
# median NSE of each gauge's twelve monthly means
grp <- unique(g[c("station_number", "area_class", "lake")])
grp$lake <- ifelse(grp$lake %in% TRUE, "lake outlet", "not a lake outlet")
validate <- function(mod, ids) {
  x <- data.frame(station_number = g$station_number, month = g$month, obs = g$obs_mm, mod = g[[mod]])
  wet_flow_validate(x[g$station_number %in% ids, ], grp[grp$station_number %in% ids, ])$summary
}
gw <- validate("wb_mm", ann$station_number)
gr <- validate("routed_mm", ann$station_number)
gw_all <- validate("wb_mm", sk$station_number)
nse_g <- function(s, g, v) one(s$nse_month_median[s$group == g & s$value == v])
# Moriasi and others' (2007) reading of a monthly score, each band open below
# and closed above (0.75 is "good"), unsatisfactory under 0.50
nse_bands <- c(satisfactory = 0.50, good = 0.65, `very good` = 0.75)
nse_rating <- function(x) c("unsatisfactory", names(nse_bands))[findInterval(x, nse_bands, left.open = TRUE) + 1]
stopifnot(identical(nse_rating(c(0.5, 0.65, 0.75, 0.76)), c("unsatisfactory", "satisfactory", "good", "very good")))
# the score is taken over one gauge's twelve months, is 1 at a perfect match
# and 0 at the gauge's annual mean in every month
x <- both$obs_mm[both$station_number == both$station_number[1]]
stopifnot(length(x) == 12, wet:::wet_nse(x, x) == 1, abs(wet:::wet_nse(x, rep(mean(x), 12))) < 1e-12)

fmt_year <- function(s) {
  c(pct1(s[["mae"]]), signed(s[["bias"]], 1), paste(signed(s[["lo"]]), "to", signed(s[["hi"]])), pct(s[["within"]]))
}
fmt_month <- function(med, d, col, s) {
  lo <- which.min(med)
  hi <- which.max(med)
  nse <- nse_g(s, "all", "all")
  c(sprintf("%.2f (%s)", nse, nse_rating(nse)),
    sprintf("%s (%s) to %s (%s)", signed(med[lo]), month.abb[lo], signed(med[hi]), month.abb[hi]),
    pct(100 * mean(abs(d[[col]] - 1) <= band)))
}
score_tab <- data.frame(
  ` ` = c("**Yearly**: mean absolute error", "Bias (mean error)", "Middle half of errors",
          sprintf("Within ±%d%%", err_cut),
          "**Monthly**: median Nash–Sutcliffe efficiency", "Median error, lowest and highest month",
          sprintf("Gauge-months within ±%d%%", err_cut)),
  rt = c(fmt_year(s_rt), fmt_month(smv("pcic_routed", 1:12, "median"), both, "ratio_r", gr)),
  wb = c(fmt_year(s_wb), fmt_month(sh$median, both, "ratio_wb", gw)),
  wb_all = c(fmt_year(s_all), fmt_month(smv("wet_balance", 1:12, "median"), bal, "ratio_wb", gw_all)),
  check.names = FALSE
)
names(score_tab)[2:4] <- c(sprintf("Routed PCIC, %d gauges", n_both),
                           sprintf("Open water balance (held out), %d gauges", n_both),
                           sprintf("Open water balance (held out), all %d", nrow(sk)))
# the prose: month by month the two score about the same on the gauges both
# are scored at (median NSE within 0.05, gauge-months within the band within 5 points)
within_m <- function(col) 100 * mean(abs(both[[col]] - 1) <= band)
stopifnot(abs(nse_g(gr, "all", "all") - nse_g(gw, "all", "all")) < 0.05,
          abs(within_m("ratio_r") - within_m("ratio_wb")) < 5)
# every gauge both are scored at counts in the NSE (none under wet_flow_validate()'s min_obs)
stopifnot(nse_g(gw, "all", "all") > 0, gw$n[gw$group == "all"] == n_both, gr$n[gr$group == "all"] == n_both,
          gw_all$n[gw_all$group == "all"] == nrow(sk))

# the prose, gauge by gauge
none <- sk[is.na(sk$routed_mm), ]
mae_of <- function(i) mean(abs(sk$err_pct[i]))
mae_head <- mae_of(sk$nesting == "headwater")
mae_nest <- mae_of(sk$nesting == "nested")
small_km2 <- 100
large_km2 <- 1000
mae_small <- mae_of(sk$area_km2 < small_km2)
mae_large <- mae_of(sk$area_km2 >= large_km2)
zone_mae <- sort(tapply(abs(sk$err_pct), sk$zone, mean))
worst <- names(zone_mae)[length(zone_mae)]
worst_name <- to_title(map$zones$name[map$zones$zone == worst])
n_worst <- sum(sk$zone == worst)
# routed PCIC is closer at most gauges; headwater gauges score worse than
# nested, small basins worse than large, and the worst zone is a semi-arid
# interior plateau (15, 17, 23 or 24: research/water_balance_method.md) that
# stands out at twice the average; the gauges without routed flow are mostly
# in the Liard (10x)
stopifnot(n_rt_closer > n_both / 2, s_rt[["mae"]] < s_wb[["mae"]], mae_nest < mae_head, mae_small > mae_large,
          sum(zone_mae > 2 * s_all[["mae"]]) == 1, worst %in% c("15", "17", "23", "24"), length(worst_name) == 1,
          nrow(none) > 0, mean(startsWith(none$station_number, "10")) > 0.5)
# the balance's median monthly error is within 10% in every month, and within
# the band at fewer than half its gauges in every month; where a gauge's
# observed flow (not monthly volume) peaks in May or June the balance falls
# short in that month at most of them
wb_med <- smv("wet_balance", 1:12, "median")
bal$obs_q <- bal$obs_mm / days[bal$month + 1]
pk <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(bal, bal$station_number), function(x) x[which.max(x$obs_q), ]))
pk <- pk[pk$month %in% 5:6, ]
stopifnot(max(abs(wb_med)) < 10, max(smv("wet_balance", 1:12, "within")) < 50, 100 * mean(pk$ratio_wb < 1) > 50,
          100 * (stats::median(pk$ratio_wb) - 1) < 0)
# routed is low in spring and high in summer, at the median and at most of its gauges
r_spring <- 3:5
r_summer <- 7:8
season_med <- function(mo) 100 * (stats::median(both$ratio_r[both$month %in% mo]) - 1)
by_g <- function(mo) tapply(both$ratio_r[both$month %in% mo], both$station_number[both$month %in% mo], mean)
g_low <- by_g(r_spring) < 1
g_high <- by_g(r_summer) > 1
stopifnot(all(smv("pcic_routed", r_spring, "median") < -10), all(smv("pcic_routed", r_summer, "median") > 10),
          season_med(r_spring) < -10, season_med(r_summer) > 10,
          identical(names(g_low), names(g_high)), length(g_low) == n_both_gauges,
          mean(g_low) > 0.5, mean(g_high) > 0.5)
# by monthly score, the balance is the stronger source on basins under 1,000
# km2, routed on those over it and at lake outlets
small_a <- c("<100 km2", "100-1000")
large_a <- c("1000-10000", ">10000")
stopifnot(all(vapply(small_a, function(k) nse_g(gw, "area_class", k) > nse_g(gr, "area_class", k), NA)),
          all(vapply(large_a, function(k) nse_g(gr, "area_class", k) > nse_g(gw, "area_class", k), NA)),
          nse_g(gr, "lake", "lake outlet") > nse_g(gw, "lake", "lake outlet"),
          nse_g(gw, "lake", "lake outlet") < nse_g(gw, "lake", "not a lake outlet"))

sm$date <- mid(sm$month)
sm$source <- factor(sm$source, names(pal_src$values))
cap_err <- paste0(
  "Error in mean monthly flow by month: the median (line) and the middle half of gauges (band), as a ",
  "percentage of the gauge's ", base_text, " mean. The water balance is held out at all ",
  n_bal_gauges, " calibration gauges; routed PCIC at the ", n_both_gauges,
  " it is scored at. Dashed lines mark ±", err_cut, "%."
)
```

Routed PCIC's yearly flow is the closer of the two at `r n_rt_closer` of the
`r n_both` gauges both are scored at. Month by
month the two score about the same, and routed PCIC errs with the season.
Each source is scored against a gauge's mean annual runoff and monthly means
over its complete years in `r base_text`: the balance at the `r nrow(sk)`
HYDAT gauges it is built on, and routed PCIC at `r n_both` of them. Error is modelled minus observed, as a percentage of observed.
The balance is scored *held out*: each Water Survey sub-sub-drainage (such as
08EE) is left out of the fit in turn and predicted from the rest, so a gauge's
neighbours in the same sub-sub-drainage cannot vouch for it. Routed PCIC is scored on the
segment each gauge snapped to: `r n_routed` gauges have routed flow, less
`r length(far)` whose segment carries under a fifth of the gauge's flow, which
the routed comparison leaves out and attributes one by one.

```{r score-table}
note_score <- c(
  "PCIC does not list the gauges it calibrated to, so its errors may be partly in sample.",
  paste0("Nash–Sutcliffe efficiency (<a href=\"#ref-nash_sutcliffe1970Riverflow\">Nash and Sutcliffe 1970</a>): how much closer a source's twelve months come to ",
         "the gauge's than a flat line at the gauge's annual mean. 1 is a perfect match; 0 is no closer than ",
         "the flat line. Ratings follow <a href=\"#ref-moriasi_etal2007Modelevaluation\">Moriasi and others (2007)</a>: very good above ",
         sprintf("%.2f, good above %.2f, satisfactory above %.2f.", nse_bands[["very good"]], nse_bands[["good"]],
                 nse_bands[["satisfactory"]]))
)
# format = "html" and kable_styling() before footnote(): a footnote on a bare
# kable in a bookdown document numbers the caption twice and writes "NA" into
# the table's style attribute (kableExtra 1.4.0); escape = FALSE for the bold row labels
score_tab[[1]] <- sub("^\\*\\*(.*)\\*\\*", "<strong>\\1</strong>", score_tab[[1]])
knitr::kable(score_tab, format = "html", align = "lrrr", row.names = FALSE, escape = FALSE,
             caption = "Error at the calibration gauges, in mean annual runoff and in the twelve mean monthly flows.") |>
  kableExtra::kable_styling(full_width = FALSE) |>
  kableExtra::footnote(general = note_score, general_title = "", escape = FALSE)
```

```{r error-month, fig.height = 4.2, fig.cap = cap_err}
ggplot(sm, aes(date)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey40") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = c(-1, 1) * err_cut, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey60") +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = q25, ymax = q75, fill = source), alpha = 0.18) +
  geom_line(aes(y = median, colour = source), linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(aes(y = median, colour = source), size = 1.3) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = pal_src$values[-1], labels = pal_src$labels[-1], name = NULL) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = pal_src$values[-1], labels = pal_src$labels[-1], name = NULL) +
  scale_x_date(date_breaks = "1 month", date_labels = "%b",
               limits = as.Date(c("2001-01-01", "2001-12-31")), expand = c(0.01, 0)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = function(x) paste0(x, "%")) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Error in mean monthly flow")
```

Where each is weak:

- **The season, routed PCIC.** It is low from March to May and high in July
  and August, as if its melt started late and ran on. Each half holds at
  most of its gauges, not only at the median (low in spring at
  `r pct(100 * mean(g_low))`, high in summer at `r pct(100 * mean(g_high))`),
  so it is the model's, not the placement's: a misplaced outlet changes one
  gauge's flow; it would not lower the spring at most gauges and raise the
  summer at most of them.
- **Spread, the balance.** Across all `r n_bal_gauges` gauges its median
  monthly error is within ±10% in every month, but in no month are half of the
  gauges within ±`r err_cut`%.
  Where a gauge's flow peaks in May or June, the balance more often falls
  short in that month than overshoots.
- **Headwaters and small basins, the balance.** It averages `r pct(mae_head)`
  yearly error at headwater gauges, whose basin holds no other gauge, against
  `r pct(mae_nest)` at nested ones, and `r pct(mae_small)` on basins under
  `r small_km2` km² against `r pct(mae_large)` on those over
  `r num(large_km2)` km². By monthly score it is still the stronger source
  under 1,000 km².
- **The dry interior, the balance.** In zone `r worst`, the `r worst_name`, its
  `r n_worst` gauges average `r pct(zone_mae[[worst]])`: runoff there is a
  small remainder of precipitation, so a small error in evapotranspiration is
  a large one in runoff.
- **Large basins and lake outlets, the balance.** By monthly score routed
  PCIC is the stronger source over 1,000 km² and at lake outlets, whose flow
  a lake holds back and releases later in the year:
  routing follows the lake, and the balance's donor gauges are matched
  without regard to it.
- **The Liard, routed PCIC.** It has no value at `r nrow(none)` gauges, most
  of them in the Liard, where the balance is the only estimate.

## Flow in a timing window, from months or from days

```{r windows}
# the gauge's daily record, as the station-flow article reads it: the mean
# over each window, in each 1981-2010 year with enough of the window's days
ws <- wet_window_stats(dh[dh$station_number %in% c("08EE013", "08EE003"), c("station_number", "date", "q_m3s")],
                       windows, stats = "mean")
# a window's mean from monthly means, wet_flow_window(): each day takes its
# month's mean. The sources' months once per gauge; the observed months per
# window, since each window has its own years
src_w <- wet_flow_window(bs[bs$station_number %in% c("08EE013", "08EE003"), c("station_number", "source", "month", "q_m3s")],
                         windows, by = c("station_number", "source"))
stopifnot(all(src_w$basis == "monthly"))
src_q <- function(s, src, w) src_w$q_m3s[src_w$station_number == s & src_w$source == src & src_w$window == w]
# the same windows from the published days (segment_daily), the same call
sd <- vm$segments_daily
sd <- sd[sd$station_number %in% c("08EE013", "08EE003"), c("station_number", "source", "doy", "q_m3s")]
src_d <- wet_flow_window(sd, windows, by = c("station_number", "source"))
stopifnot(all(src_d$basis == "daily"))
src_qd <- function(s, src, w) src_d$q_m3s[src_d$station_number == s & src_d$source == src & src_d$window == w]
win <- do.call(rbind, lapply(c("08EE013", "08EE003"), function(s) {
  do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(windows)), function(k) {
    w <- windows[k, ]
    yrs <- ws$year[ws$station_number == s & ws$period == w$window]
    # the observed months over the same years as the daily means
    mo <- my[my$station_number == s & my$year %in% yrs, ]
    om <- stats::aggregate(q ~ month, mo, mean)
    obs_w <- wet_flow_window(data.frame(month = om$month, q_m3s = om$q), w, by = character())
    data.frame(station_number = s, window = w$window, span = paste(md_text(w$start), "–", md_text(w$end)),
               years = length(yrs),
               daily = mean(ws$value[ws$station_number == s & ws$period == w$window]),
               obs_months = obs_w$q_m3s,
               routed = src_q(s, "pcic_routed", w$window),
               balance = src_q(s, "wet_balance", w$window),
               routed_daily = src_qd(s, "pcic_routed", w$window),
               balance_daily = src_qd(s, "wet_balance", w$window))
  }))
}))
stopifnot(!anyNA(win), all(win$years >= min_years))
approx_err <- 100 * (win$obs_months / win$daily - 1)
err_of <- function(col) 100 * (win[[col]] / win$daily - 1)
# what the days do to a window: each source's move from its months to its
# days, beside the gauge's own move from its monthly means to its daily record
move_of <- function(src) 100 * (win[[paste0(src, "_daily")]] / win[[src]] - 1)
win$move_obs <- 100 * (win$daily / win$obs_months - 1)
win$move_routed <- move_of("routed")
win$move_balance <- move_of("balance")
# the approximation per window, at its worse gauge
approx_w <- tapply(abs(approx_err), win$window, max)[windows$window]
good_w <- names(approx_w)[approx_w < 5]
poor_w <- names(approx_w)[approx_w >= 5]
in_poor <- win$window %in% poor_w
at <- function(s, w = poor_w) win$station_number == s & win$window %in% w
wp <- function(col, s) one(win[[col]][at(s)])
ep <- function(col, s) one(err_of(col)[at(s)])
# the reason the prose gives for the poor window: the second half of July
# runs well below July's mean
late_july <- vapply(c("08EE013", "08EE003"), function(st) {
  x <- dh[dh$station_number == st & dh$month == 7, ]
  mean(x$q_m3s[as.integer(format(x$date, "%d")) >= 15]) / mean(x$q_m3s)
}, 0)
# the prose, sentence by sentence. Good windows: the gauge's daily record and
# its monthly means agree within 5%, and the days move no source's window by
# more than a tenth. The poor window is fry migration alone, and there the
# monthly means overstate the gauge by about a quarter at both gauges. Routed
# PCIC's days fall faster than the gauge's, and its error shrinks at both. The
# balance's days at Buck Creek fall as the gauge's do (its donor is itself),
# leaving its annual error; at Houston they fall less than half as far, and
# the balance stays several times the gauge in both late-summer windows
late_w <- c("Spawning", "Fry migration")
# the prose: migration spans whole months (May 1 to Aug 1, both days counted
# by wet_flow_window()) and costs under 1%; spawning starts on a month and
# ends mid-month
stopifnot(identical(windows$start[windows$window == "Migration"], "05-01"),
          identical(windows$end[windows$window == "Migration"], "08-01"), approx_w[["Migration"]] < 1,
          identical(windows$start[windows$window == "Spawning"], "08-01"),
          identical(windows$end[windows$window == "Spawning"], "09-15"),
          identical(good_w, c("Migration", "Spawning")))
b003 <- err_of("balance_daily")[win$station_number == "08EE003" & win$window %in% late_w]
stopifnot(identical(poor_w, "Fry migration"), all(late_july < 0.9),
          max(approx_w[good_w]) < 5, all(abs(c(win$move_routed, win$move_balance)[!in_poor]) < 10),
          all(approx_err[in_poor] > 20), all(approx_err[in_poor] < 30),
          all(win$move_routed[in_poor] < win$move_obs[in_poor]),
          all(abs(err_of("routed_daily")[in_poor]) < abs(err_of("routed")[in_poor])),
          abs(wp("move_balance", "08EE013") - wp("move_obs", "08EE013")) < 1,
          abs(ep("balance_daily", "08EE013") - wb_off[["08EE013"]]) < 2,
          wp("move_balance", "08EE003") < 0,
          abs(wp("move_balance", "08EE003")) < abs(wp("move_obs", "08EE003")) / 2,
          length(b003) == 2, all(b003 > 200))
```

Read from monthly means, every day of a timing window takes its month's mean. That costs almost nothing where a timing window spans whole months, as migration
does from 1 May to 1 August, and
little where the month it cuts changes slowly: spawning ends mid-September,
and the gauge's own monthly means and daily record agree within
`r sprintf("%.0f%%", approx_w[["Spawning"]])`. `r and_text(poor_w)` takes the
second half of July, as the freshet recedes, and there the monthly means
overstate the gauge by about a quarter.

The published days remove that cost where a source's daily pattern is right.
Routed PCIC's fry-migration error shrinks at both gauges. The balance's days
at Buck Creek fall with the gauge's, since its pattern there is the gauge's
own, and only its annual error remains. At Houston its borrowed pattern keeps
more water into late summer, and the balance stays several times the gauge
in both late-summer timing windows. That error is ours.

```{r window-table}
tab <- data.frame(
  Gauge = st_label[win$station_number], `Timing window` = paste0(win$window, " (", win$span, ")"),
  Years = win$years,
  `Daily record (m³/s)` = sprintf("%.1f", win$daily),
  `Months vs days` = signed(approx_err),
  `Routed PCIC, months` = signed(err_of("routed")),
  `Routed PCIC, days` = signed(err_of("routed_daily")),
  `Water balance, months` = signed(err_of("balance")),
  `Water balance, days` = signed(err_of("balance_daily")),
  check.names = FALSE
)
tab$Gauge[duplicated(tab$Gauge)] <- ""
knitr::kable(tab, row.names = FALSE, align = "llrrrrrrr",
             caption = paste0("Flow in each chinook life history timing window, ", base_text,
                              ". Daily record: the gauge's own daily flow, averaged over the timing window in each year with enough of its days. Months vs days: the same ",
                              "years' observed monthly means, read as a timing window, against the daily record. Each source ",
                              "twice, from its published months and from its published days, as its difference from ",
                              "the daily record."))
```

## Limits

```{r limits}
# the coverage bullet: basins other than the Liard have balance parts and no routed part
no_rt <- setdiff(seg_parts$code[seg_parts$source == "wet_balance"], seg_parts$code[seg_parts$source == "pcic_routed"])
stopifnot(length(no_rt) > 1)
# the bullet: the adjustment ships although the headwater gate does not pass
# (a recorded override, #43), and pooled zones get none
stopifnot(isTRUE(ps$keep_adjust), isFALSE(ps$gate_pass), identical(ps$pooled_variant, "none"))
```

- **Coverage.** Besides the Liard, routed PCIC has no value in a few northern
  and border basins, and only some on the outer coast's islands.
- **The zone adjustment is kept by decision.** On headwater basins it does
  not beat raw precipitation less evapotranspiration, and zones with too few
  gauges for their own adjustment get none.
- **Segments without a value.** The balance reaches a segment through
  `fwapg`'s lookup matching segments to watershed polygons, and both sources
  are published only on matched segments, so the `r pct_of(sg[["no_lut"]])` of
  segments matched to none have no value.
- **In-sample at the gauges.** On a calibration gauge's own segment the
  published balance is the gauge's own monthly pattern at the balance's
  annual flow (08NM240 and 08NM241, on one watershed, share the mean of
  theirs). A watershed much like a gauge gets almost the same pattern.
- **Days.** A day is right only as far as the source's daily pattern is,
  and the scores above are of the months; the balance's daily pattern is
  scored where it was fitted, not here.
- **Houston** (08EE003) is seasonal: its monthly means cover `r m003_text`,
  from `r n003` of the years `r base_text`.
- **The monthly scores are province-wide**, split by basin size and lake
  outlets, not by region or zone.

## Software and citation

The flows in this article, the routed values at the gauges and the picks on
the map are the published product's, read on `r format(ps$built)` from the
build at `wet` commit `r pub$wet_commit`. Before they were written, routed
PCIC's values were held equal to `fwapg`'s routed table and its days at the
Bulkley gauges were routed again from the sub-basin days there, and the
balance's months and days were made again from the fit at
`r paste(pm$shape_stations, collapse = " and ")`; the build's own check of
its published flows, [its report](`r gh(pub$report)`), covers the rest. The
province shares are from the segment table that build was cut from. The
gauges' daily flows are HYDAT's. The scores compare routed PCIC as
published, and the balance held out by its fit on HYDAT
`r substr(ps$hydat_release, 1, 10)`, with HYDAT's observed runoff.

```{r provenance}
# Provenance. Gauge values were read on ps$built from the published build
# pub$wet_commit (segment table pub$segment_commit) and checked against their
# sources by data-raw/segment_vignette_data.R at wet commit ps$wet_commit;
# the picks on the map, from the same build, by data-raw/segment_vignette_map.R
# at map$provenance$wet_commit; the Bulkley segments' months and days and the
# gauges' held-out months by data-raw/monthly_vignette_data.R at pm$wet_commit
# (daily fingerprint pm$daily_fingerprint, pm$daily_report). Gauge scores are
# from province run ps$province_run (annual AET ps$aet, HYDAT release
# ps$hydat_release), routed PCIC from fwapg at ps$routed_commit
# (ps$routed_fingerprint), scored in ps$routed_report; the province counts are
# ps$segment_report's, whose segment table (ps$segment_report_commit) the
# build's checked tree was cut from, every part byte-identical to the
# published build's.
stopifnot(nzchar(ps$wet_commit), nzchar(map$provenance$wet_commit), nzchar(pm$wet_commit), nzchar(ps$routed_commit))
```

The product is made with the PostgreSQL tools [`fwapg`](https://smnorris.github.io/fwapg/)
[@norris2024smnorrisfwapg] and New Graph's
[fork](https://github.com/NewGraphEnvironment/fwapg/tree/newgraph) of it
[@norris_irvine2026NewGraphEnvironmentfwapg], and the R package
[`wet`](https://newgraphenvironment.github.io/wet/) [@irvine2026wetStream]; the balance's inputs come
through [`climr`](https://github.com/bcgov/climr) [@daust_etal2024climr] and
[`cd`](https://newgraphenvironment.github.io/cd/) [@irvine2026cd]; the recipes above read it with
[`duckdb`](https://r.duckdb.org/) [@muhleisen_raasveldt2026duckdb], and the figures are drawn with
[`ggplot2`](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/) [@wickham2016ggplot2],
[`gq`](https://newgraphenvironment.github.io/gq/) [@irvine2026gq] and
[`sf`](https://r-spatial.github.io/sf/) [@pebesma_bivand2023Spatial]. How the balance is built, and each of its choices tested:
[the water balance method](`r gh("research/water_balance_method.md")`). To cite this package:

```{r citation, results = "asis"}
cat(format(utils::citation("wet"), style = "text"), sep = "\n\n")
# the Data line names the shipped annual AET (CGIAR floored by Fu-Budyko) and
# the snow predictors in the monthly shares; the fork's commit is the one
# segment-discharge.bib carries (its References line)
bib <- readLines(file.path(dirname(knitr::current_input(dir = TRUE)), "segment-discharge.bib"), warn = FALSE)
stopifnot(identical(ps$aet, "cfu"), identical(pm$share_spec, "snow"),
          any(grepl(sprintf("version = {%s}", ps$routed_commit), bib, fixed = TRUE)))
```

### Data

- The product: `s3://fresh-bc/discharge/fwa/v1/`. The bucket allows no listing,
  so a reader starts from its manifest, <`r pub$manifest`>, as
  `wet_catalog()` does. This article reads the build of `r built_text`.
- Routed flow: the Pacific Climate Impacts Consortium, University of Victoria
  ([hydromosaic](https://beehive.pacificclimate.org/chyp/): VIC-GL hydrologic
  model output routed with Raven, PNWNAmet forcing), placed on the Freshwater
  Atlas by New Graph's fork of `fwapg` [@norris_irvine2026NewGraphEnvironmentfwapg].
- Stream network: the Province of British Columbia's Freshwater Atlas Stream
  Network, through DataBC [@flnrord2021FreshwaterAtlasb].
- Gauge records: the Water Survey of Canada's HYDAT
  [@environmentandclimatechangecanada2021NationalWater], release
  `r substr(ps$hydat_release, 1, 10)`.
- Climate normals, 1981–2010, for the balance: the R package
  [`climr`](https://github.com/bcgov/climr) [@daust_etal2024climr].
- Actual evapotranspiration, for the balance: CGIAR-CSI's Global
  High-Resolution Soil-Water Balance v3
  ([figshare 7707605](https://figshare.com/articles/dataset/Global_High-Resolution_Soil-Water_Balance/7707605)),
  held no lower than a Fu–Budyko estimate.
- Elevation: the Copernicus GLO-90 DEM.
- Snow, for the balance's monthly shares: ERA5-Land snow normals (Copernicus
  Climate Change Service), through the R package
  [`cd`](https://newgraphenvironment.github.io/cd/) [@irvine2026cd].
- Hydrologic zones: the province's BC Hydrologic Zones.
- Life history timing windows for chinook salmon: New Graph's species-timing
  table [@gottesfeld_rabnett2007SkeenaFish].

```{r wordcount, include = FALSE}
f <- knitr::current_input()
if (!is.null(f)) {
  x <- readLines(f, warn = FALSE)
  y <- utils::tail(x, -utils::head(which(x == "---"), 2)[2])   # drop the YAML header
  cite <- which(y == "## Software and citation")
  stopifnot(length(cite) == 1)
  y <- utils::head(y, cite - 1)   # the closing citation section is not body prose
  fence <- cumsum(grepl("^```", y)) %% 2 == 1
  y <- y[!fence & !grepl("^```", y)]
  y <- gsub("`r [^`]*`", "", y)          # inline code is not body prose
  y <- y[!grepl("^\\s*$", y)]
  n <- sum(lengths(strsplit(trimws(y), "\\s+")))
  message("body prose: ", n, " words")
  cap <- 2000
  if (n > cap) stop("body prose is ", n, " words; the cap is ", cap)
}
```
